newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: SOCCER-POBORSKY, BERGER VOTED CZECH FOOTBALLERS OF YEAR.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-POBORSKY, BERGER VOTED CZECH FOOTBALLERS OF YEAR.

text.p: Euro 96 Czech soccer stars Karel Poborsky and Patrik Berger were voted joint winners of the Czech footballer of the year award on Sunday night in Prague.

Poborsky, who has had a troubled start with his new club Manchester United, looked bewildered as he recieved the prize while Liverpool's Patrik Berger was unable to attend because of Monday's top of the table premiership clash with Newcastle.
Poborsky was swept into the limelight of European soccer after a series of dazzling performances in Euro 96, helping the Czech Republic to the finals where they lost to Germany in extra time.

But he has struggled to reproduce that form at Manchester United following his transfer this summer from Czech league champions Slavia Prague, a problem which has been exacerabated by his inability to speak English.
At Sunday's ceremony, the moderator referred to media speculation that Poborsky was living through "hell" in England beacuse he could not commmunicate with players or management.
"Do you know what the English word for "hell" is?" asked the moderator.
"No. I don't speak English," Poborsky replied.

In contrast, his Czech international team mate Patrik Berger has made a solid contribution to Liverpool's league title challenge this season after his transfer from 1995 German league champions Borusia Dortmund after the Euro 96.
The prize was awarded on the basis of votes from Czech football league managers, sports journalists and the Czech -Moravian Football Association.
